prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There’s no single “best” contractor for everyone — the right Miami roofing company depends on your exact needs (residential vs. commercial, budget, roof type) and whether they can show the proper hurricane-rated materials and local approvals. I can find and shortlist top local contractors for you if you tell me your ZIP or address. Meanwhile, use the checklist below to identify a top hurricane-rated roofer in Miami.

What to require for hurricane-rated roof replacement
- Miami‑Dade County/Florida approvals: Materials and systems should have Miami‑Dade Notice of Acceptance (NOA) or Florida Product Approval. Ask for the NOA number for the product and system used.  
- Proper license and insurance: Verify the contractor’s Florida roofing license/DBPR registration and current general liability and workers’ comp insurance.  
- Installer/manufacturer certifications: Look for manufacturer‑certified installers (GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Preferred, Firestone/TPO certified, etc.).  
- Permits & code compliance: Contractor must obtain building permits and follow the current Florida Building Code (high‑wind/hurricane requirements).  
- Proven hurricane experience: Ask for references and photos from completed hurricane‑rated jobs in Miami-Dade or other high‑wind areas.  
- Written warranties: Distinguish manufacturer material warranties vs. contractor workmanship warranties (ideally multi‑year and transferable).  
- Proper fastening & flashing details: Uplift-rated attachments, enhanced perimeter & penetration details, and correct underlayment/roof deck prep per NOA.

How to verify quickly
- DBPR license lookup (Florida Department of Business & Professional Regulation) to confirm license status.  
- Ask for the Miami‑Dade NOA numbers for the roofing materials and installation system and verify via Miami‑Dade Product Control.  
- Check reviews: Google, BBB, Angi/HomeAdvisor, and local Facebook/Nextdoor for recent experiences.  
- Request proof of insurance (COI), and call the insurer to confirm.  
- Get 3 detailed bids and compare scope, not just price.

Questions to ask every contractor
- Are you licensed in Florida and registered for Miami‑Dade work? Can you provide license number?  
- Which roofing system and products will you use? Please provide Miami‑Dade NOA numbers.  
- Are you certified by the manufacturer? Can I see proof?  
- Will you pull permits and handle inspections?  
- What's included in the contract (tear‑off, deck repairs, underlayment, flashing, cleanup, dumpster)?  
- Warranties: manufacturer vs. workmanship — length and transferability.  
- Can you provide recent local references and photos of completed hurricane‑rated projects?  
- How is payment scheduled? (Avoid large upfront cash payments.)

Red flags
- No Miami‑Dade NOA or unwillingness to provide NOA/product approval.  
- Pressure to sign immediately or requests for large cash deposits.  
- Vague or verbal-only warranties.  
- No proof of insurance or license.  
- Extremely low bid far below others (often corners are cut).

If you want, I can:
- Look up and shortlist 3–5 well‑rated Miami roofing contractors that meet hurricane/NOA requirements (I’ll need your ZIP or neighborhood).  
- Provide an email/template you can send to contractors to request bids and the specific documentation above.

Which would you prefer — a shortlist for your area, or the bid-request template?
